redFirst.basis: `python3 plugins/audit/tests/test_verify_invariants.py --selftest` in a throwaway tree at HEAD exited 1 with 2 of 71 collected tests failing an assertion, the task's own among them (HEAD's own tests green on HEAD's code), each passing with the working tree's implementation - rw9 (house FAIL), rw10 (house FAIL): SELFTEST FAILED: 69/71 cases passed; run without CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, OLDPWD, PWD; dependencies linked from the project root, entry by entry as symlinks: node_modules - .cache, .vite, .vite-temp are not linked and a new entry a runner makes beside the links stays in the throwaway, but a write into a linked entry lands in the project's own node_modules and is not watched; the user's .npmrc in the home directory dropped (every run has a fresh home)

outcome.technical: _pull_rebases in _invariants.py now reads --rebase=<value> as git does: false/no/off/0/empty (case-insensitive) are not a rebase, any other value is; single-dash letter clusters (-r, -qr) request rebase iff r precedes any of s/X/o/j. rw9 gained =no, =OFF, =0, -q -s ours, -sr as clean; rw10 gained =true, =interactive, =yes, -qr as rewrites. Selftest 71/71 pass, exit 0; ruff clean; vermin ok.
outcome.descriptive: An explicit pull --rebase=no no longer raises a false history-rewrite breach; short clusters like -qr are now seen.

claims: claims: _pull_rebases matches git's boolean-or-mode reading for the listed spellings, evidenced by rw9/rw10 passing in test_verify_invariants.py --selftest (71/71, exit 0).
